name: remap
description: Your world awaits. Remap turns the time you have into a ride, run, walk or hike worth remembering, through the quiet roads, trails and scenery around you, anywhere on Earth.

interface.longDescription:
Your world awaits.

There’s always another way out: a quiet road beneath the trees, a path beside the water, a climb that changes the whole afternoon. Tell Remap how far you want to go or how long you have, and it turns that into somewhere worth going. Road cycling, gravel, running, trail running, walking and hiking, anywhere on Earth.

Remap looks beyond the fastest line to what gives each stretch its character: how quiet it is, how busy it gets, whether it follows a river or the coast, whether it winds through forest or parkland. Fresh routes appear on a map right in the chat within seconds, with the climbs ahead and the scenery waiting along the way. Or name where you want to end up, and Remap shapes the journey there, split into days on a bike tour.

Ask for shorter, longer, flatter or hillier, more of the landscapes you love, or quieter roads. When one feels right, tap Ride, Run, Walk or Hike and take it out with the Remap app.

Connect your Remap account and Remap gets to know you: the activities you do, how far and how hilly you like to go, and the places that matter to you. Then a simple "find me a ride" already fits. Save a route for later, and look back over your recent activities and saved routes. Connecting is optional: every route works without an account.
capabilities: Generates cycling, bike touring, running, trail running, walking and hiking routes
Generates routes to a destination, and bike tours split into days
Starts from a place or your location
Shows routes on a map with their stories
Opens a route in the Remap app
Remembers your activities, preferences and places when you connect your account
Saves routes to your Remap account and lists your activities and saved routes
defaultPrompt: A 40 km bike ride from the Ferry Building in San Francisco, as flat as possible.
Find me a 45 minute trail run from where I am, through forest.
A hilly 15 km hike from Ambleside in the Lake District.

positive.description: A cycling request with a start place and a distance.
positive.prompt: Find me a 40 km bike ride starting at the Ferry Building in San Francisco.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls generate_routes with start the Ferry Building, sport cycling and distance 40 (in km). The map shows routes of about 40 km starting and finishing at the Ferry Building, each listed with distance, time and climbing, and the text result carries a link that opens the same request in Remap.

positive.description: A trail running request from the person's current location.
positive.prompt: Find me a 45 minute trail run from where I am, through forest.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls generate_routes with sport trail_running, duration_minutes 45 and environments including forest, and no start. The map asks for the person's location and generates trail runs of about 45 minutes from there; the model does not ask for a start in the chat as well.

positive.description: A hiking request with a start place, a distance and climbing.
positive.prompt: A hilly 15 km hike from Ambleside in the Lake District.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls generate_routes with start Ambleside, sport hiking, distance 15 (in km) and climbing hilly. The map shows hiking routes of about 15 km starting and finishing in Ambleside.

positive.description: An ambiguous start the model confirms first.
positive.prompt: Where exactly is Victoria Park? I want to cycle 30 km from there.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls find_place for Victoria Park and lists the matches with their places, then asks which one. Reply "The one in London": it then calls generate_routes with that place's lng and lat, sport cycling and distance 30, and the map shows routes of about 30 km starting at Victoria Park in London.

positive.description: A trip from a start to a destination.
positive.prompt: A bike trip from Amsterdam to Brussels, about 100 km a day.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls generate_routes with start Amsterdam, destination Brussels, sport cycling and distance 100 (in km, the longest day), and no climbing or environments. The map shows a trip from Amsterdam to Brussels split into days, and the text result carries a link that opens the same trip in Remap.

positive.description: Remembering preferences in the person's Remap account, then a route that leaves them open.
positive.prompt: Remember that I mostly ride a road bike, about 40 km, on quiet roads. Then make me a loop.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls update_profile; without a connected account it asks the person to connect their Remap account (sign in with the test account), then saves the activity, distance and quiet roads and reads the profile back. It then calls generate_routes with no distance or sport, and the map shows road cycling loops of about 40 km from the person's location, never from a saved place unless they name it.

positive.description: Saving a generated route to the person's Remap account.
positive.prompt: Save the second route to my Remap account, then list my saved routes.
positive.expected_behavior: After routes are on the map, calls save_route for the second route, then list_saved_routes; the saved route is listed with its name and distance. Asks to connect the account first if it is not connected.

negative.description: A driving request: Remap generates routes for riding, running, walking and hiking only.
negative.prompt: What is the fastest way to drive from Berlin to Munich?

negative.description: A gear question with no route to generate.
negative.prompt: Which bike should I buy for commuting?

negative.description: A general fitness question with no route to generate.
negative.prompt: How many calories does a 10 km run burn?

publication.release_notes: Connect your Remap account (optional): Remap remembers your activities, preferences and places, saves routes to your account, and answers questions about your recent activities and saved routes. The map now also shows each route's busy stretches and climbs.
